summary: A dense, multi-column interior page of the Daily Inter Mountain (Butte, Montana) for St. Patrick's Day weekend, 1889. The page mixes local editorial commentary, legal notices, classified advertising, entertainment listings, and a substantial volume of display advertising from Butte merchants. Editorial matter dominates the left-hand columns with pieces on the mine inspector bill, copper output, Irish affairs, and Montana's produce price house; the right-hand columns fill rapidly with commercial display ads for clothing, lime, dry goods, minstrel shows, grocery firms, jewelers, and patent medicines. The overall tone is boosterish and commercially active, reflecting a prosperous mining-town readership on the eve of St. Patrick's Day.

clipping_placements.placement_note: display ad occupying a mid-page block beneath the Maguire's Opera House minstrel notice, flanked left by editorial columns and right by merchant ads

juxtapositions: The AOH Grand Ball advertisement, with its Irish-Catholic committee of Harrington, Murphy, Driscoll, and Hennessy, sits directly below a prominent advertisement for 'Goodyer, Cook & Dillens' Refined Minstrels' at Maguire's Opera House, placing an Irish fraternal society's St. Patrick's Day celebration cheek-by-jowl with a commercial minstrel-show promotion.

The St. Patrick's Day editorial in col 1, which invokes the patriotism and suffering of old Ireland, runs on the same page as the copper-output column discussing the Anaconda syndicate's grip on Montana mining — quietly yoking Irish national sentiment to the industrial economy that employed Butte's largely Irish workforce.
